task_production_rates.name: Inspect Ceiling Drywall Surface

QT2.notes: Note only major defects (holes, large ridges)

QT3.notes: Identify and mark all visible defects

QT4.notes: Comprehensive overhead inspection under bright light

QT5.notes: Critical inspection with raking light, multiple passes

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walking inspection overhead with work light. Bare drywall — looking for mud defects, unfilled joints, damaged paper. Slower than wall inspection due to overhead neck angle.

defect_tolerance.QT2: Note holes and large ridges only. Minor mud imperfections acceptable.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Mark all visible defects including ridges, debris, unfilled joints.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Mark all imperfections visible under bright work light.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Mark every defect visible under raking light. Multiple passes required.

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum Drywall Dust from Ceiling
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: HEPA vacuum with brush attachment on extension pole, overhead. Slower than wall vacuum — overhead work, dust falls into face/eyes. Must be thorough — dust causes adhesion failure on primer.

defect_tolerance.all: Surface must be dust-free. Adhesion failure from residual dust is a binary fail.

task_production_rates.name: Protect Ceiling Openings and Fixtures
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Stuff and tape ~8 ceiling openings per room (6 recessed light locations + 2 electrical box locations). Mix of installed cans/boxes and open holes. ~15 min per room.

defect_tolerance.all: All openings sealed — no gaps where insulation or overspray can pass. Binary pass/fail.

task_production_rates.name: Pin Plastic Over Window Openings
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lightweight plastic pinned over window openings — not intricate masking. Tape top edge, let plastic hang. ~3 min per window.

defect_tolerance.all: Plastic covers opening to catch fallout. Does not need to be airtight.

task_production_rates.name: Pin Plastic Over Door Openings
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lightweight plastic pinned over door openings. Larger than windows, may need to work around installed exterior doors. ~5 min per opening. Typically only exterior doors at this NC phase.

defect_tolerance.all: Plastic covers opening to catch fallout. Does not need to be airtight.

task_production_rates.name: Lay Rosin Paper Floor Protection (Hard Floors)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Unroll rosin paper, tape all edges and seams with 2-inch masking tape. Full coverage, zero tolerance for gaps. Includes cutting around obstacles.

defect_tolerance.all: Full coverage, all seams taped, no gaps. Binary pass/fail — any exposed finished floor is a fail.

task_production_rates.name: Lay Floor Protection (Carpeted Floors)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Lay canvas drop cloths or plastic sheeting over carpet. Faster than rosin paper — no taping of seams required, just overlap and weight down.

defect_tolerance.all: Full coverage of carpeted areas. Overlap seams adequately.

task_production_rates.name: Roll Ceiling Primer
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 18-inch roller with extension pole overhead. Single coat primer on bare drywall. No edge work — primer overlaps onto wall area. Porous bare drywall absorbs product and creates more roller drag than primed/sealed surfaces. Overhead work ~15% slower than equivalent wall rolling.

defect_tolerance.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier. Surface must be uniformly sealed. (Note: surface condition imperfections such as mud ridges or drywall defects are governed by the inspection task's defect tolerance, not the application task.)

task_production_rates.name: Roll Ceiling Primer (Textured)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 18-inch roller with 1/2 to 3/4 inch nap on textured ceiling. Texture absorbs more product and requires slower pace to fill valleys. Porous bare drywall compounds the absorption. Overhead work.

defect_tolerance.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier. All texture valleys must be filled and sealed. (Surface condition imperfections governed by inspection task tolerance.)

task_production_rates.name: Spray Ceiling Primer
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray overhead on bare porous drywall. Coupled to backroll rate — spray cannot outrun backroller. Rate shown is spray component; system throughput is limited by backroll rate.

defect_tolerance.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier. Even coverage with proper mil thickness. (Surface condition imperfections governed by inspection task tolerance.)

task_production_rates.name: Backroll Ceiling Primer
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: 18-inch roller on extension pole, immediately following spray. Consolidates primer into drywall, eliminates air pockets, levels finish. Sets pace for spray+backroll system — this is the bottleneck. Bare porous drywall absorbs product and creates more drag than a sealed surface, making primer backroll SLOWER than finish coat backroll.

defect_tolerance.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier. Primer must be fully consolidated into surface. (Surface condition imperfections governed by inspection task tolerance.)

task_production_rates.name: Vacuum Floors After Ceiling Prime
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Shop vacuum of floor to remove primer drips and overspray debris. On subfloor: direct vacuum. On finished floors: vacuum over rosin paper, inspect paper integrity.
task_production_rates.notes: PROPOSED NEW KEY — PS_META.SF.FLOOR_VACUUM_AREA not yet in catalog.

defect_tolerance.all: Floor clear of debris and primer drips. On finished floors, rosin paper intact.

task_production_rates.name: Remove Ceiling Opening/Fixture Protection
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove paper and tape from ceiling openings/fixtures. Faster than setup — just pull.

defect_tolerance.all: All protection material removed from ceiling openings.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Tools
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fixed time per job to clean rollers, spray equipment. Primer cleanup is water-based — straightforward. Spray equipment takes longer than rollers alone.

defect_tolerance.all: Tools cleaned and stored or disposed properly.

task_production_rates.name: Final Ceiling Prime Inspection

QT4.notes: Detailed overhead inspection with bright light

QT5.notes: Critical inspection with raking light — surface must be uniform

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Walking inspection of primed ceiling. Touch up holidays or missed spots. Primer inspection is checking for coverage and seal — not cosmetic perfection (that's the finish coat's job).

defect_tolerance.QT2: Confirm full coverage — no bare drywall visible.
defect_tolerance.QT3: Confirm full coverage, no holidays. Touch up any missed areas.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Confirm uniform coverage under bright work light. No thin spots, holidays, or drips.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Confirm uniform coverage under raking light. Surface must be ready for high-build finish system.

quality_tier_effects.description: Economy ceiling prime — reduced inspection, single prime coat
quality_tier_effects.notes: Economy: quick inspection, single coat primer, basic final check. Application quality is NOT reduced — a properly applied coat is still required.

quality_tier_effects.description: Standard ceiling prime — baseline for all rates
quality_tier_effects.notes: Standard NC: thorough inspection, single coat primer, thorough final check.

quality_tier_effects.description: Premium ceiling prime — more thorough inspection and verification
quality_tier_effects.notes: Premium: detailed inspection, single coat primer with mil thickness verification, detailed final inspection. Still single coat — primer coat count does not vary by QT.

quality_tier_effects.description: Critical ceiling prime — critical inspection, high-build primer
quality_tier_effects.notes: Critical: critical inspection with raking light, high-build primer (single coat), critical final inspection. Surface must be ready for semi-gloss+ finish system.

texture_effects.notes: Baseline — smooth new drywall (Level 4 or 5 finish)
Orange peel texture increases surface area ~15%, slows application ~15%
Knockdown texture increases surface area ~25%, slows application ~20%

coupling_constraints.description: When using spray+backroll, spray rate must not exceed backroll rate. Backroller sets the pace.

validation.status: PASS — spray 400 > backroll 300, system limited to 300 SF/hr

coupling_constraints.practical_implication: Spray at 400 SF/hr, backroll at 300 SF/hr means effective ceiling prime rate is 300 SF/hr per 2-person crew
coupling_constraints.notes: Spray and backroll done by 2-person crew working in tandem. Bottleneck is backroll. Primer backroll is slower than finish coat backroll due to porous surface absorption.

crew_configurations.name: Ceiling Primer Roller
crew_configurations.notes: One person rolls ceiling primer with 18-inch roller on extension pole.

crew_configurations.name: Spray + Backroll Ceiling Prime Crew
crew_configurations.notes: Sprayer and backroller work in tandem. Backroller sets pace.

overhead_factor.description: Ceiling work is inherently slower than equivalent wall work due to overhead neck angle, arm fatigue, and gravity working against you
overhead_factor.notes: Ceiling rates are approximately 15% slower than equivalent wall work rates. Already baked into the per-task rates above.

height_effects.notes: Standard residential ceiling. Extension pole from floor.
May require step ladder or scaffolding for some tasks.
Scissor lift or scaffolding tower required.

risks.risk: Primer backroll rate on porous drywall may vary significantly by drywall level and primer viscosity
risks.mitigation: Field calibrate. Rate range 250-350 allows adjustment.

risks.risk: Ceiling opening count heuristic (8 per room) varies significantly by home design
risks.mitigation: Heuristic flagged. Engine should allow per-room override when actual counts available.

risks.risk: Rosin paper floor protection rate untested
risks.impact: Floor protection time may be over/under-estimated
risks.mitigation: Field calibrate. Rate is estimate based on unroll + tape workflow.
